A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, proofs, and experimental appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia summarization experiments, including GPT-4o winrates, reward-model validation results, best-of-N evaluations, and controlled ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original summarization experiments in Figures 3–6 and Appendix A, including comparisons of offline and online DPO and local versus global reward models.

M1.justification: The training procedures remain unchanged: offline and online DPO, local/global reward models, and batched online preference construction using the highest- and lowest-ranked of 25 completions. The theoretical revisions do not introduce a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TL;DR summarization, GPT-labeled preferences, two-word summaries, and ROUGE-L-based preferences. The new maze figure illustrates the mechanism explanation; it is not presented as an additional training or evaluation benchmark.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same SFT, offline DPO, and online DPO comparators, including the two-epoch DPO control where previously used. Reward-model comparisons still include DPO, Local, and Global models. The removed SPIN theorem was not an empirical baseline comparison.

E3.justification: v2 removes the regularized-objective evaluation using an on-policy reverse-KL estimate and the training-data-fraction sweep associated with v1 Figures 4 and 12. Retained experiments have unchanged splits, sampling temperatures, training settings, and evaluation sample counts in v1 Appendix B and v2 Appendix C.

E4.justification: Two supporting analyses disappear: the check that the online advantage persists without GPT-4o evaluation and the sensitivity study varying preference-data quantity. The prompt-augmentation, label-distribution, reward-model type/size, two-word, and ROUGE-L analyses remain, with several relocated to Appendix A.

E5.justification: Figure 3 changes its three-seed statement from 'all DPO variants' to 'all methods,' extending the stated coverage to SFT. This is a reporting change, not evidence of additional runs. The other three-seed statements and best-of-N standard-error reporting are retained.

E6.justification: v2 omits v1 Figure 4's regularized-objective results, including 0.685 versus 0.797 for 1.4B and 0.777 versus 0.853 for 2.8B, and Figure 12's dataset-fraction results. Matched retained results are unchanged, including Figure 3 winrates, two-word scores of 6.3/21.9/23.2, and ROUGE-L scores of 0.354/0.352/0.358.

T1.justification: v2 removes the linear-SPIN/SFT equivalence theorem and its proof (v1 Theorem 2.4 and Appendix A.4). It rewrites Theorems 2.2–2.3 and their proofs explicitly over sets of optima. Theorem 3.1 becomes Theorem 4.1 with revised realizability conditions and a substantially rewritten proof. These change formal scope and assumptions beyond notation or relocation.

C1.justification: The main equivalence and generation-verification/proper-learning claims remain. However, the introduction no longer claims the SPIN–SFT equivalence as a contribution, narrowing the demonstrated theoretical coverage. The abstract foregrounds sample efficiency, which was already part of v1's H6.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 expands the mechanism account through maze navigation, effective horizon, and trading computation for preference data. v2 also adds an argument excluding reward-variance explanations and removes the infinite-data discussion accompanying v1 Figure 12. Its statement that competing hypotheses were falsified is stronger than v1's account and conflicts with Appendix A.5's explicit admission that H5 was not falsified.

D1.justification: The project-release statement changes from an aim to open-source code, models, and data to a commitment conditional on paper acceptance. Neither version documents an actual project release. Dataset instructions, prompts, hyperparameter tables, hardware, training-time information, and existing resource links otherwise match.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to Xiao et al. on concurrent information-geometric characterization, Razin et al. on reward-model variance, Laidlaw et al. on effective horizon, and Chandrasekaran and Jordan on computational-statistical tradeoffs. Several references accompanying removed material disappear. The central positioning relative to DPO and inverse reinforcement learning remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: H1–H5 move from Section 3.1 to Appendix A, generation-verification gaps become a separate main section, and the remaining appendices shift accordingly. Extensive paragraph rewrites, new navigation text, and an expanded isomorphism explanation reshape how the argument is presented.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column preprint layout, with extensive figure repositioning, resizing, and caption restructuring. v1 Figures 4 and 12 disappear, several retained plots move to Appendix A, and v2 adds the maze illustration as Figure 7. The dataset and hyperparameter tables retain their contents while being reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the optimizer-set statements more explicit and clarifies H6 through the expanded Section 4.2. However, removing v1 Figures 4 and 12 reduces evidence concerning evaluator dependence and sample efficiency, while the stronger claim that alternatives were falsified conflicts with Appendix A.5. These gains in explanation coexist with reduced empirical support and less careful interpretation, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
